title: feat(rules): add SS-008 checked-arithmetic detector for storage values
problem: Contract entry points perform unchecked `+`, `-`, `*` on values read from storage or supplied as parameters. On overflow these panic in debug or wrap/abort depending on the build, and Soroban provides `checked_add`/`checked_sub`/`checked_mul` for explicit handling.
why: Silent arithmetic errors can corrupt balances and accounting; explicit checked math turns an undefined outcome into a typed contract error.
scope: Detect binary arithmetic operators in public `#[contractimpl]` functions where an operand is a storage read or a function parameter.
Ignore operations on clearly bounded local counters.
Report the operator expression as evidence with a suggested checked alternative.
guidance: Reuse `rules::util::facts_from_block` to collect method calls and add binary-expression facts (operator, operands).
Use `syn::ExprBinary` visiting; record the operator token and the rendered operand text.
Keep confidence low until type flow exists; do not claim overflow is reachable.
acceptance: Positive fixture triggers; negative fixture using `checked_add` does not.
tests: Unit test for the detector with inline sources.
False-positive test for bounded local arithmetic.
security: Findings are heuristic; never assert exploitability.
dod: Rule registered, documented, fixtured, tested, and CI green.

title: feat(rules): add SS-009 insecure randomness detector
problem: Contracts may derive randomness from `env.ledger().timestamp()` or `ledger().sequence()`, which are predictable and attacker-influenced by transaction submission timing.
why: Predictable randomness enables manipulation of lotteries, selection, and any value-dependent logic.
scope: Flag entry points that use `ledger().timestamp()` / `ledger().sequence()` in arithmetic or comparisons that appear to select an outcome.
Exclude timestamps used purely for expiry checks when the comparison target is a stored deadline.
guidance: Add ledger-accessor facts to `rules::util` (method chain containing `ledger`).
Combine with the presence of modulo or comparison operators to reduce noise.
acceptance: Negative fixture using a stored deadline does not trigger.
security: Heuristic; confidence low. Must not claim a concrete exploit.
dod: Rule merged with documentation and fixtures.

title: feat(rules): add SS-010 missing-events detector for privileged operations
problem: Privileged state changes (admin changes, parameter updates, pausing) are performed without emitting an event, removing the off-chain audit trail.
why: Events are how indexers and users observe critical changes; missing events reduce accountability and incident response.
scope: Detect storage mutations in entry points that look privileged (admin/owner/pause/params keys) with no `env.events().publish` call.
Keep the privileged-key heuristic explicit and configurable.
guidance: Match storage key literals/`symbol_short!` values against a configurable list.

title: feat(rules): add SS-011 re-initialization detector
problem: A contract exposes an `initialize`-style function that writes configuration without checking whether it has already been initialized, allowing an attacker to re-initialize and take over.
why: Re-initialization is a common high-impact vulnerability in upgradeable/initializable contracts.
scope: Detect functions named `initialize`/`init` that mutate storage with no prior existence check (`has`, `get` + early return).
Support an explicit one-time guard via constructor as a negative case.
guidance: Look for storage `has`/`get` guards and `#[contracttype]` initialization flags.
acceptance: Both constructor and flag-guard negatives covered
security: High severity, medium confidence; state reachability assumptions in docs.

title: feat(rules): add SS-012 unbounded Vec growth detector
problem: Entry points push into a storage-backed `Vec`/`Map` with no cap, growing ledger entries without bound.
why: Unbounded growth increases rent and eventually makes reads/iteration fail, a denial of service.
scope: Detect `push_back`/`push_front`/`set` on a value read from storage followed by a write-back, with no length check.
Negative case: a capped collection.
guidance: Combine storage read + mutation facts; check for a `len()` comparison guard.

title: feat(rules): add SS-013 cross-contract call before state update detector
problem: An entry point makes a cross-contract call before updating its own state, allowing a malicious callee to re-enter and observe/exploit inconsistent state.
why: Soroban permits reentrancy; ordering matters for multi-contract invariants.
scope: Order cross-contract constructors/calls relative to storage mutations within a function.
Flag calls that precede the first relevant state write.
guidance: Use byte spans to order AST call facts and mutation facts.
Be conservative: only flag when both occur in the same function.
security: High severity, low confidence; document limitations clearly.

title: feat(rules): add SS-014 token transfer amount validation detector
problem: Token transfers use an amount parameter with no validation that it is positive and within bounds.
why: Negative or absurd amounts can drain or corrupt balances depending on token semantics.
scope: Detect `transfer`/`transfer_from` calls whose amount argument is an unchecked parameter.
guidance: Detect the call, then check whether a comparison against zero guards the amount.

title: feat(rules): add SS-015 deprecated Soroban SDK version detector
problem: The project depends on an old `soroban-sdk` major version with known API or security fixes.
why: Staying current avoids known issues and unsupported behavior.
scope: Parse the declared `soroban-sdk` version requirement and compare against a documented minimum.
Report at the manifest with the declared version as evidence.
guidance: Emit a manifest-level finding; do not require source parsing.
Make the minimum configurable and documented.
acceptance: Manifest-level findings supported by the engine
tests: Unit test with a synthetic manifest
security: Informational; severity depends on the policy.
deps: Engine currently requires a source location; a manifest location may be needed.

title: feat(rules): add SS-016 instance-storage-for-unbounded-data detector
problem: Large or growing collections are stored in instance storage, which is loaded for every invocation and has strict size limits.
why: Misusing instance storage increases cost and can break the contract at scale.
scope: Flag repeated instance-storage `set` of distinct keys or collection growth.
guidance: Distinguish constant instance config from growing data via key variability.

title: feat(rules): add SS-017 authorization-after-mutation detector
problem: A function mutates state before calling `require_auth`, so the authorization check runs after the effect.
why: State changed before the check can persist on some paths and indicates a logic ordering bug.
scope: Order `require_auth` facts against storage mutation facts within an entry point.
guidance: Use spans to compare positions; only flag mutation strictly before auth.

title: feat(rules): reduce SS-002 false positives via client address provenance
problem: SS-002 flags any unauthenticated cross-contract constructor, including calls to a hardcoded, trusted contract address or a stored admin-configured address.
why: False positives erode trust and cause teams to disable the rule.
scope: Track whether the client address argument is a hardcoded literal, a storage read, or an untrusted parameter.
Downgrade or suppress the finding when the address is trusted configuration.
guidance: Extend `CallFact` to capture argument provenance for constructors.
acceptance: SS-002 documentation updated with the provenance logic
Fixtures for trusted vs untrusted addresses
security: Do not reduce true-positive detection; add negatives only where justified.
dod: Merged with corpus updates and green CI.

title: feat(rules): add rule categories filter to configuration
problem: Rules can only be enabled/disabled individually; teams cannot disable a whole category (for example all low-confidence heuristics).
why: Category-level control is a common and convenient policy mechanism.
scope: Add `[rules] disabled_categories = ["resource-usage"]` and `enabled_categories`.
Validate category names during config validation.
guidance: Apply category filters in `RuleRegistry`/engine before severity overrides.
acceptance: Unknown category is a usage error
